transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As we all know, we want to preserve several of our older relatives' stories in recordings that future family members can listen to and watch. I've got the only working camcorder, so I'm coordinating the recording evening and will be making the final call on how the files are handled afterward. We've got the family shared digital drive available for storing everything. Before we finalize any plans, I'd like to hear from each of you individually. Nina, could you go first? Please share any preferences, advice, or constraints you have about the recording evening or how the files should be handled. I'll record your response before we move on. Omar, I'll ask you next.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important. My grandmother told me she's willing to be recorded only if the interviews stay in the family archive and are not posted publicly online. I haven't had a chance to relay this to anyone yet, but I think it's really important we respect her wishes as we plan the recording evening and decide how the files are handled.

She recommended that the audio should be captured as uncompressed WAV files at exactly 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, and that we should make two verified backup copies. I think this would really help ensure the recordings are preserved properly for the family.
